description: A glide selector whose list opens smoothly and whose raised pill slides onto the next option with a springy glide; dragging a finger across the list works too.
interactionNotes: A click or `Space`/`Enter` opens the list and the raised pill lands on the active option. Move over the list with the pointer or the arrow keys so the pill glides with a spring; pressing and dragging a finger does the same and, with the release velocity, advances several rows. `Escape` closes it and typing the first letter jumps to the option whose name starts with it.

props.options: The options; a string or an object `{ value, label, tag }`.
props.onChange: Called on selection and returns the option itself too.
props.placeholder: Text shown when nothing is selected.
props.showTags: Whether the small tag beside the options is shown.
props.accentColor: Color of the check on the selected option.
props.textColor: Text color of the button and the options.
props.size: Size of the button and the rows.
props.radius: Roundness of the button and the menu, pixels.
props.menuWidth: Minimum width of the menu, pixels.
props.placement: Whether the menu opens above or below the button.
props.align: Which edge to stick to; it mirrors automatically in RTL.
props.popDuration: Duration of the menu opening, milliseconds.
props.glideDuration: Duration of the pill gliding between options, milliseconds.
props.rememberPosition: When the pointer leaves the list, the active position is kept.
props.autoPreview: Site preview only: it opens the menu, glides the pill to the next option, and selects it — all through the real open/glide/select path.

tips: `tag` holds a short note, not the name: in the file-template demo, `label` stays the Latin "PNG" and `tag` is "without quality loss". The two sit in separate elements and `tag` lives in an isolated left-to-right domain, so it does not mix with Persian text.

Do not think of `align` physically: under `dir="rtl"` the value `left` means "stick to the start edge", which is the right side. The component mirrors it itself, so you do not need to change anything by hand.
For a list with more than eight options, make `menuWidth` larger and do not pass `tag`; tight rows get crowded with a tag next to the name.
The motion is not only `motion` — most of the opening and closing is CSS keyframes, so it has no noticeable cost even across dozens of selectors on one page.
